subject: Clarify: token apportionment across long/short prompts and minimums
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexaapps.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexaapps.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify token accounting for mixed prompt lengths and minimums

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our technical team has a follow-up on billing mechanics that will determine whether we lock in the 12-month commit. Two points they asked us to confirm:

1) If a request contains a 2k-token system + 200-token user prompt + 50-token model response, how are tokens bucketed for the per-call minimum?
2) For streaming endpoints, what rounding rules apply per-call vs per-minute aggregates? We have a lot of short label-generation calls mixed with long-context summarization; the invoice math needs to be predictable.

I've attached a short CSV with representative request mixes. Can you confirm (or put us in touch with billing) so we can finalize the SOW?

Appreciate it —
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Integrations, NexaApps
Elena.Torres@nexaapps.com

Attachment: nexa-workload-samples.csv (stub, 12KB)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexaapps.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify token accounting for mixed prompt lengths and minimums

Elena —

Thanks for the samples, that helps a lot. Short answers up front, longer below:

- Per-call minimums are applied after tokenization of the entire request+response for that call (system+prompt+response). If you hit the streaming endpoint and the response is emitted in chunks, we still aggregate tokens consumed for that single logical request before applying the per-call floor.
- Rounding: we bill in 10-token quanta for hosted customers by default. That means each call is rounded up to the next 10-token increment before any per-call minimum is evaluated.

Longer explanation and a worked example:

Example request from your CSV: system=2000, prompt=200, model output=50 => total = 2250 tokens. Rounded up to next 10-token quantum => 2250 (already divisible by 10). If your plan has a 500-token per-call minimum (unlikely at this scale), we'd still charge 2250 because it's above the minimum. If instead the call were system=50, prompt=40, response=10 => 100 tokens rounded to 100; if minimum is 200 tokens per call, you are billed 200.

For mixed workloads we recommend a hybrid approach in the contract: 
1) Commit to an annual token volume (reduces per-token price) and
2) Put short-call smoothing in the commit (e.g., 60% of short-call usage can be amortized into the commit's microburst pool) so you avoid excessive per-call minimums on label-generation traffic.

Vanessa, Kimberly — can you confirm the exact quantum and sample math we should send to Elena and include the proposed pricing matrix?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexaapps.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify token accounting for mixed prompt lengths and minimums

Elena —

Quick follow-up with concrete numbers based on your CSV (see attached pricing matrix):

- Default quantum: 10 tokens (hosted). For enterprise Dedicated/Private we can make it 1 token in the SLA but that requires an ops adjustment and slightly higher base price.
- Example rows (from CSV):
  * Summarization call (2k system + 400 prompt + 300 response): raw 2700 -> billed 2700 tokens.
  * Short label call (50 sys + 40 prompt + 10 response): raw 100 -> rounded -> 100 -> if per-call minimum is 250 -> billed 250.

Proposal to mitigate pain for you:
1) Offer a microburst reserve of 2M tokens that acts as a smoothing pool for short calls during heavy bursts. Short calls get consumed from the microburst pool first, avoiding per-call minima until the pool is exhausted.
2) For the annual commit (we discussed 120M tokens), we'll grant a 15% discount on the standard hosted per-token rate and waive per-call minimums for label-generation endpoints (up to 1.8M tokens/year). After that threshold, per-call minima apply.

This keeps your invoicing predictable for the mixed profile you shared. Kimberly — can you confirm feasibility and the wording we should include in the SOW around "waive per-call minima for specified endpoints up to X tokens"?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-pricing-matrix.xlsx (stub, 45KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexaapps.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify token accounting for mixed prompt lengths and minimums

Hi Elena —

I looked over the workload CSV and Vanessa's draft. Operational notes and suggested contract language below so your legal/procurement can review: 

Operational behavior (confirmed):
- Tokenization timing: tokens are counted at response finalization for request-level billing semantics. Streaming chunking does not create separate billable units; we aggregate tokens for the logical request.
- Rounding quantum: hosted = 10 tokens; Dedicated = configurable to 1 token (requires a Dedicated SKU and minor runtime config).
- Per-call minimums: applied post-rounding. Example phrase: "Per-call minimums, where specified in the pricing schedule, shall be applied to the total token count for each logical request after tokenization and rounding to the applicable quantum."

Contract SOW language (suggested, copy-friendly):
"Redwood shall apply per-logical-request token accounting. Each logical request's total tokens (system + prompt + response) will be rounded up to the nearest [quantum] token increment prior to application of any per-call minimums. For this engagement, the quantum is 10 tokens for Hosted API usage. The Parties agree that per-call minima shall be waived for endpoints listed in Schedule A (Labeling APIs) up to an aggregate annual allowance of 1,800,000 tokens; excess label-generation usage shall be billed subject to standard per-call minima and per-token rates."

Billing example table (short):
- Call A: 2,250 raw -> rounded 2,250 -> billed 2,250
- Call B: 95 raw -> rounded 100 -> per-call minimum 250 -> billed 250
- Microburst pool: consumed before per-call minima; when exhausted, calls revert to per-call minima behavior.

If you want, we can include a small clause to allow quarterly re-calibration of the microburst pool (transfer 10% of unused microburst to subsequent quarter) — that helps when you underutilize the smoothing pool.

If that looks acceptable I can draft the pricing appendix and SOW language for legal review; please confirm which endpoints should be in Schedule A.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexaapps.com>

Thanks, team — this is exactly what procurement and engineering needed. Two quick items before we loop legal:

1) Please mark the label-generation endpoints (POST /v1/labels, POST /v1/tagging/batch) as Schedule A.
2) Can you put the microburst pool and the 15% commit discount into a short term-sheet we can sign (we want to avoid prolonged SOW redlines)? If you can send that by end of day Friday we'll route to legal + procurement early next week.

If you send a one-page term-sheet I can get internal approval quickly.

Appreciate everyone's help.
Elena
Head of Platform Integrations, NexaApps
